avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce immune dysregulation or interfere with antiretroviral efficacy through CYP450 effects on other HIV medications
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consult HIV specialist before use

avoid_supplements.name: Echinacea
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potential immunostimulation may complicate HIV disease management and viral load monitoring
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid or use only under medical supervision with close CD4/viral load monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Probiotics
caution_supplements.mechanism: May influence gastrointestinal absorption and immune function; generally safe but monitor response
caution_supplements.action: Use standard formulations; inform provider of use during routine monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D
caution_supplements.mechanism: HIV patients often deficient; supplementation supports immune function without direct interaction
caution_supplements.action: Appropriate supplementation encouraged with baseline and periodic monitoring

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: Enfuvirtide is administered subcutaneously (no oral bioavailability); food interactions minimal but general nutrition important for immune status
caution_foods.action: Maintain balanced nutrition; no specific dietary restrictions required for drug efficacy

monitoring_notes: Enfuvirtide undergoes minimal hepatic metabolism and has no significant CYP450 interactions, making supplement/food interactions less critical than with other antiretrovirals. Monitor for injection site reactions and maintain overall immune health through proper nutrition and avoid immunosuppressive supplements.
